name: hero-color-panel
title: Hero Color Panel
description: A split landing hero with a big two-line headline, short paragraph, pill button and two tech badges on the left, and a block of floating horizontal colour panels on the right. The stacked bars slide and blend like a soft moving gradient.
use: A product landing page wants an abstract, always-moving colour visual next to its headline without using video.
avoid: The shader animates without pause and needs WebGL, and its fixed neon palette can fight a muted brand.
a11y: A screen-reader h1 names the hero and the button carries text, but the endless shader never stops for reduced-motion users. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: On black, a left column stacks a large white two-line heading, a small grey paragraph, an outlined pill button and two bordered badges. The right visual is a loose pile of horizontal rounded bars in lime, mint, violet, magenta and green that fade to black at their tips.
behaves: The stacked bars glide sideways at different speeds, each sliding out of and back into the pile, so the block keeps reshaping. The text and buttons hold still, hover lifts the button and badges, and on small screens the bars move to a dimmed strip under the copy.
customise: Set heading, subtitle, description, CTA and badges as props, and tune the shader with colours, density, speed and angles. Layout changes are classes.
weight: heavy: A full-time WebGL colour-panel shader redraws half the hero every frame.
